proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof (rate), stated for a general graph piece with radii gamma_1 < gamma_2 (the parent uses gamma_1 = gamma, gamma_2 = gammahat, c_1 = c_0/2, C_0 = max(C_7, 0)). It uses the children monotonicity_bounds, graph_comparison, radial_height, tilt_height_l1, rescaled_varifold, pinching, tilt_iteration, campanato and tangent_ae; the hypotheses TiltExcessDecayTheorem and ConicalApproximationTheorem are passed to tilt_iteration and pinching. Notation: mu := V.weight, p_y := V.tangentProj y, |.| Hilbert-Schmidt norm (hsNorm), ||.|| operator norm (||A|| <= |A| <= sqrt(n) ||A|| for A : R^n -> R^l), a := 1/(2n+2), alpha' := 1 - n/p in (0,1), kappa := (p-n)/(4p), Lambda := delta/kappa, omega_n := unitBallVolume n, Omega := B^o_{gamma_2 rho}(0) (open ball of R^n), F(x) := q(graphPoint(x, u x)), T_0 := rotatedPlane q (an n-dimensional subspace, the image of R^n x {0} under the isometry q) with orthogonal projections P_0 and Q_0 := I - P_0 (so dist(y, T_0) = |Q_0 y| and Q_0 F(x) = q(graphPoint(0, u x))), and for linear A : R^n -> R^l, G_A := q(span{graphPoint(v, A v)}) (G_0 = T_0). B_s closed and B^o_s open balls; E(z,s,T) := V.tiltExcess z s T, K(z,s) := V.scaledLpNorm H p z s.

0. Linear algebra.
 (Nor) For linear A and w in R^l: |q(graphPoint(0, w)) - p_{G_A} q(graphPoint(0, w))| >= |w| (1 + ||A||^2)^(-1/2). [q is an isometry, so this is the distance from graphPoint(0, w) to span{graphPoint(v, A v)}, which is inf_v (|v|^2 + |w - A v|^2)^(1/2); and |w| <= |w - A v| + ||A|| |v| <= (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2) (|w - A v|^2 + |v|^2)^(1/2).]
 (Ang) For linear A: ||A|| <= (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2) ||p_{G_A} - P_0||. [If A = 0 this is trivial. Otherwise take a unit v with |A v| = ||A|| and e := q(graphPoint(v, A v))/(1 + |A v|^2)^(1/2), a unit vector of G_A; then P_0 e = q(graphPoint(v, 0))/(1 + |A v|^2)^(1/2), so (p_{G_A} - P_0) e = e - P_0 e = q(graphPoint(0, A v))/(1 + |A v|^2)^(1/2), of norm ||A||/(1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2).]
 (Gp) There is L_0 = L_0(n,l) in (0, 1/4] with |A - B| <= |p_{G_A} - p_{G_B}| whenever |A|, |B| <= L_0. [Pi(A) := projection onto span{graphPoint(v, A v)} has the block form [[(I + A^T A)^-1, (I + A^T A)^-1 A^T], [A (I + A^T A)^-1, A (I + A^T A)^-1 A^T]] (the minimiser v of |x - v|^2 + |y - A v|^2 solves (I + A^T A) v = x + A^T y), a smooth (rational) function of A with DPi(0)[B] = [[0, B^T], [B, 0]], so |DPi(0)[B]| = sqrt(2) |B|; there is C_g = C_g(n,l) >= 1 with |DPi(X) - DPi(0)| <= C_g |X| for |X| <= 1 (operator norm between the Hilbert-Schmidt spaces; Pi is C^2 on the compact ball |X| <= 1, and C_g may be enlarged to be >= 1). For |A|, |B| <= L_0 := min{1/4, (sqrt(2) - 1)/C_g}, the mean value inequality for Pi - DPi(0) on the segment [B, A] gives |Pi(A) - Pi(B)| >= (sqrt(2) - C_g L_0)|A - B| >= |A - B|. Conjugation by q preserves Hilbert-Schmidt norms and p_{G_A} = q Pi(A) q^-1.]

1. Constants (chosen before U, V, H, delta, rho, q, u). Let delta_E be given by graph_comparison for (n, l, p), and C_rad > 0 by radial_height for n (it depends only on n and serves every l). Put C_c := e^2 omega_n (1 + 1/kappa) + e/kappa and C_u := 2 e^2 (1 - gamma_2)^(-n) + 2e/omega_n. Let (delta_6, C_II°, C_III°) be given by tilt_iteration with c_l := 1/2 and c_u := C_u. The contract of tilt_iteration says nothing about the signs of C_II° and C_III°, so we normalise: C_II := max{C_II°, 1} and C_III := max{C_III°, 1}; thus C_II >= 1 and C_III >= 1, and step 6 shows that the conclusions of tilt_iteration remain true with C_II°, C_III° replaced by C_II, C_III. Only the normalised constants C_II, C_III are used below. Put eps_1 := min{1/4, delta_6} > 0, and let (delta_P, cs) be given by pinching with (gamma_2, eps_1) (admissible: 0 < gamma_2 < 1 and 0 < eps_1 <= 1/4); so 0 < cs <= (1 - gamma_2)/16. Put gamma' := (gamma_1 + gamma_2)/2, c_r := min{(gamma_2 - gamma')/4, (1 - gamma_2)/4}, c_sig := min{c_r/2, eps_1 cs/2}, c_s := min{c_sig, gamma' - gamma_1}, C_H := C_0 + C_rad (log(gamma_2/c_1) 2^(n+4) C_c)^(1/(n+1)) (>= 0 because C_0 >= 0, C_rad > 0 and log(gamma_2/c_1) > 0), C_E := 2^n [144 C_u omega_n (2 C_H/c_r)^2 + 4 (C_u omega_n)^(1-1/p) (2 C_H/c_r)], C_2 := max{(c_r/(2 c_sig))^n C_E, 1}, C_D := 2 sqrt(n) (C_II C_2)^(1/2), C_Hol := (2^(2n+2+2 alpha') C_III C_2/omega_n)^(1/2) c_sig^(-alpha'), and CR := max{C_H, C_D, C_Hol, 2 C_D (2/c_s)^alpha'}. All of these are >= 0. Let delta_R > 0 be the minimum of: kappa (< 1/4), delta_E, eps_1, delta_P, delta_l := kappa min{1/4, omega_n/3} (then Lambda <= 1/4 and Lambda <= omega_n/3, so e^-Lambda (1 - Lambda/omega_n) >= (3/4)(2/3) = 1/2), delta_a := (c_r/(gamma' max{C_H, 1}))^(1/a), and delta_L := (L_0/max{C_D, 1})^(1/a). Fix U, V, H, 0 < delta <= delta_R, rho, q, u as in the statement; then 0 < delta < 1, delta <= eps_1, Lambda <= 1 and monotonicity_bounds applies.

2. Density bounds. If |y| <= gamma_2 rho then B_{(1 - gamma_2) rho}(y) is contained in B_rho(0); (M1) of monotonicity_bounds with R := (1 - gamma_2) rho, letting r -> R and using mu(B_r(y)) <= mu(B_rho(0)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n rho^n <= 2 omega_n rho^n, gives s^-n mu(B_s(y)) <= e^2 R^-n 2 omega_n rho^n + 2e = C_u omega_n, i.e. mu(B_s(y)) <= C_u omega_n s^n for 0 < s < (1 - gamma_2) rho; if moreover y is in spt V, (M2) gives mu(B_s(y)) >= e^-Lambda (omega_n - Lambda) s^n >= omega_n s^n/2 for the same s (delta <= delta_l). By (M3), the integral over B^o_rho(0) of |y - p_y y|^2 |y|^(-n-2) d mu is at most e^Lambda (e^Lambda (1+delta) omega_n + Lambda - omega_n) = e^Lambda (omega_n (e^Lambda (1+delta) - 1) + Lambda) <= C_c delta, since e^Lambda (1 + delta) - 1 <= e Lambda + e delta for Lambda <= 1 and Lambda = delta/kappa.

3. Graph facts. graph_comparison applies to Omega (open, u is C^1 on it, F(Omega) is contained in spt V cap B^o_rho(0) by hypothesis, delta <= delta_E) and gives: (E1) for Borel A contained in Omega and Borel g >= 0, the integral over A of g(F x) dx is at most the integral over F(A) of g d mu; (E2) for a.e. x in Omega, p_{F x} = p_{G_{Du(x)}}; (E3) for a.e. x in Omega, F(x) is an L^2-Lebesgue point of y -> p_y for mu (in the sense of the statement of graph_comparison). By tangent_ae (b), fix a Borel map p~ with p~ = p mu-a.e.; applying (E1) with A = Omega to the indicator of a Borel mu-null set containing {p != p~} shows that p_{F x} = p~_{F x} for a.e. x in Omega. Also u(0) = 0 and ||Du|| <= 1/7 on the convex set Omega give |u(x)| <= |x|/7, |x| <= |F(x)| <= 2|x| and |F(x) - F(x')| <= (50/49)^(1/2) |x - x'| for x, x' in Omega.

4. Height (H). For a.e. x in Omega, (E2) gives that T_x := G_{Du(x)} is the plane with p_{F x} = p_{T_x}; it contains q(graphPoint(x, Du(x) x)), and F(x) - q(graphPoint(x, Du(x) x)) = q(graphPoint(0, w)) with w := u(x) - Du(x) x. Hence F(x) - p_{F x} F(x) = q(graphPoint(0, w)) - p_{T_x} q(graphPoint(0, w)), and by (Nor) its norm is at least |w| (50/49)^(-1/2) >= |w|/2. With |x|^(-n-2) <= 2^(n+2) |F(x)|^(-n-2) this gives |u(x) - Du(x) x|^2 |x|^(-n-2) <= 2^(n+4) g(F x) for a.e. x in Omega (both sides are 0 at x = 0), where g(y) := |y - p~_y y|^2 |y|^(-n-2) (Borel; 0 at y = 0). By (E1) with A = Omega, F(Omega) contained in B^o_rho(0), g = |y - p_y y|^2 |y|^(-n-2) mu-a.e., and step 2:
 integral over Omega of |u(x) - Du(x) x|^2 |x|^(-n-2) dx <= 2^(n+4) integral over B^o_rho(0) of |y - p_y y|^2 |y|^(-n-2) d mu <= 2^(n+4) C_c delta.
 Apply radial_height (constant C_rad, for this l) with R := gamma_2 rho, r_1 := c_1 rho (< R), eps := C_0 delta^a >= 0, m := 2^(n+4) C_c delta >= 0, using ||Du|| <= 1/7 <= 1, u(0) = 0 and the near-zero hypothesis: for every x in Omega, |u(x)| <= (C_0 delta^a + C_rad (log(gamma_2/c_1) 2^(n+4) C_c delta)^(1/(n+1))) |x| <= C_H delta^a |x|, because delta^(1/(n+1)) <= delta^a for 0 < delta <= 1. (H)

5. Tilt at a fixed scale. Let z be in B_{gamma' rho}(0) (closed ball of R^n; it lies in Omega), zeta := F(z) and r_gamma := c_r rho. By (H) and delta <= delta_a, |zeta| <= |z| (1 + C_H delta^a) <= gamma' rho + (gamma_2 - gamma') rho/4. Every x in spt V cap B_{r_gamma}(zeta) satisfies |x| <= gamma' rho + (gamma_2 - gamma') rho/2 < gamma_2 rho, so x is in spt V cap B^o_{gamma_2 rho}(0) and, by hypothesis, x = F(x') with x' in Omega; then dist(x - zeta, T_0) = |Q_0(x - zeta)| = |u(x') - u(z)| <= C_H delta^a (|x'| + |z|) <= 2 C_H delta^a rho =: h. B_{r_gamma}(zeta) is contained in B_rho(0), hence in U. tilt_height_l1 with (zeta, r_gamma, h, T_0) gives
 integral over B_{r_gamma/2}(zeta) of |p_x - P_0|^2 d mu <= 144 r_gamma^-2 integral over B_{r_gamma}(zeta) of dist(x - zeta, T_0)^2 d mu + 4 h integral over B_{r_gamma}(zeta) of |H| d mu.
 As mu-a.e. point lies in spt V, the first integrand is <= h^2 mu-a.e. on the ball; mu(B_{r_gamma}(zeta)) <= C_u omega_n r_gamma^n by step 2 (|zeta| <= gamma_2 rho and r_gamma < (1 - gamma_2) rho); and by Hoelder and 2.3, the integral over B_{r_gamma}(zeta) of |H| is at most delta rho^(n/p - 1) (C_u omega_n r_gamma^n)^(1 - 1/p) <= (C_u omega_n)^(1-1/p) delta r_gamma^(n-1). Dividing by (r_gamma/2)^n and using h/r_gamma = 2 C_H delta^a/c_r and delta^(1+a) <= delta^(2a): E(zeta, r_gamma/2, T_0) <= C_E delta^(2a).

6. Decay. For z, zeta as in step 5: zeta is in spt V (hypothesis) and |zeta| < gamma_2 rho <= (1 + gamma_2) rho/2, so pinching (delta <= delta_P) gives mu(B_{cs rho}(zeta)) <= (1 + eps_1) omega_n (cs rho)^n. Let V' be given by rescaled_varifold with centre zeta and scale 1: V' is V translated by -zeta, in U' = U - zeta (open), with weight the image of mu under y -> y - zeta, support spt V - zeta, V'.tangentProj x = p_{zeta + x}, multiplicity theta(zeta + .), and generalized mean curvature H'(x) = H(zeta + x). Then V' satisfies AllardHypotheses H' p eps_1 (cs rho): cs rho > 0; the mean curvature identity holds; theta' >= 1 a.e. for the translated weight (the translation is a measurable bijection, so null sets correspond); 0 is in spt V'; B_{cs rho}(0) is contained in U' because B_{cs rho}(zeta) is contained in B_rho(0) (|zeta| + cs rho <= ((1 + gamma_2)/2 + (1 - gamma_2)/16) rho < rho); mu'(B_{cs rho}(0)) = mu(B_{cs rho}(zeta)) <= (1 + eps_1) omega_n (cs rho)^n; and K'(0, cs rho) = K(zeta, cs rho) <= K(0, rho) <= delta <= eps_1 (for nested balls B_s(z) in B_rho(0), s^(p-n) <= rho^(p-n) as p > n). Put sigma_gamma := c_sig rho, which is <= eps_1 cs rho/2. For 0 < s <= sigma_gamma, step 2 gives (1/2) omega_n s^n <= mu'(B_s(0)) = mu(B_s(zeta)) <= C_u omega_n s^n. tilt_iteration (eps_1 <= delta_6, S_0 := T_0) yields an n-plane S(zeta) with |p_{S(zeta)} - P_0|^2 <= C_II° E_2 and E'(0, s, S(zeta)) <= C_III° (s/sigma_gamma)^(2 alpha') E_2 for 0 < s <= sigma_gamma, where E_2 := V'.tiltExcessStar H' p eps_1 0 sigma_gamma T_0.
 Normalisation. E_2 >= 0: E_2 is the maximum of E'(0, sigma_gamma, T_0) and eps_1^-1 times the square of the real number K'(0, sigma_gamma).toReal, and this second entry is >= 0 (eps_1 > 0). Hence C_II° E_2 <= C_II E_2, and, since (s/sigma_gamma)^(2 alpha') E_2 >= 0, C_III° (s/sigma_gamma)^(2 alpha') E_2 <= C_III (s/sigma_gamma)^(2 alpha') E_2. Therefore |p_{S(zeta)} - P_0|^2 <= C_II E_2 and E'(0, s, S(zeta)) <= C_III (s/sigma_gamma)^(2 alpha') E_2 for 0 < s <= sigma_gamma.
 Bound on E_2. By the weight and tangent identities of rescaled_varifold, E'(0, s, S) = E(zeta, s, S) and K'(0, s) = K(zeta, s); hence E_2 = max{E(zeta, sigma_gamma, T_0), eps_1^-1 K(zeta, sigma_gamma)^2} <= max{(r_gamma/(2 sigma_gamma))^n C_E delta^(2a), eps_1^-1 delta^2} <= C_2 delta^(2a), using monotonicity of the tilt integral in the radius (sigma_gamma <= r_gamma/2), K(zeta, sigma_gamma) <= delta and delta^2/eps_1 <= delta <= delta^(2a). Multiplying E_2 <= C_2 delta^(2a) by the nonnegative numbers C_II and C_III (s/sigma_gamma)^(2 alpha'):
 |p_{S(zeta)} - P_0|^2 <= C_II C_2 delta^(2a) and E(zeta, s, S(zeta)) <= C_III C_2 (s/sigma_gamma)^(2 alpha') delta^(2a) for 0 < s <= sigma_gamma.

7. Identification on the graph. For a.e. z in B_{gamma' rho}(0) both (E2) and (E3) hold at z; then, with zeta = F(z) and small s > 0 (mu(B_s(zeta)) is positive and finite), |p_zeta - p_{S(zeta)}|^2 <= 2 mu(B_s(zeta))^-1 integral over B_s(zeta) of |p_x - p_zeta|^2 d mu + 2 mu(B_s(zeta))^-1 integral over B_s(zeta) of |p_x - p_{S(zeta)}|^2 d mu <= 2 (Lebesgue average) + (4/omega_n) E(zeta, s, S(zeta)), which tends to 0 as s -> 0 by (E3), the lower bound of step 2 and step 6. Hence p_{G_{Du(z)}} = p_zeta = p_{S(zeta)} for a.e. z in B_{gamma' rho}(0).

8. Bound on Du. For such z, (Ang) and ||Du(z)|| <= 1/7 give ||Du(z)|| <= (50/49)^(1/2) ||p_{S(zeta)} - P_0|| <= 2 |p_{S(zeta)} - P_0| <= 2 (C_II C_2)^(1/2) delta^a (step 6). Du is continuous on Omega and a full-measure subset of the closed ball B_{gamma' rho}(0) is dense in it, so this holds for every z in B_{gamma' rho}(0); therefore |Du(z)| <= sqrt(n) ||Du(z)|| <= C_D delta^a <= L_0 there (delta <= delta_L).

9. Campanato input. Let s_gamma := c_s rho. For a.e. z in B_{gamma_1 rho}(0) (as in step 7) and 0 < s <= s_gamma: B_{s/2}(z) is contained in B_{gamma' rho}(0) (gamma_1 rho + s/2 < gamma' rho), F(B_{s/2}(z)) is contained in B_s(zeta) (|F(x) - F(z)| <= (50/49)^(1/2) s/2 < s), and s <= sigma_gamma. By (Gp) (applicable by step 8), (E2), p = p~ at F(x) for a.e. x, (E1) with the Borel function y -> |p~_y - p_{S(zeta)}|^2, and step 6:
 integral over B_{s/2}(z) of |Du(x) - Du(z)|^2 dx <= integral over B_{s/2}(z) of |p_{G_{Du(x)}} - p_{G_{Du(z)}}|^2 dx = integral over B_{s/2}(z) of |p~_{F x} - p_{S(zeta)}|^2 dx <= integral over B_s(zeta) of |p_y - p_{S(zeta)}|^2 d mu(y) = s^n E(zeta, s, S(zeta)) <= A s^(n + 2 alpha'), with A := C_III C_2 sigma_gamma^(-2 alpha') delta^(2a) >= 0 (a product of nonnegative numbers, C_III >= 1).
 (The mu-integral is a genuine integral of a bounded measurable function over a ball of finite measure, by tangent_ae (b), so it equals the Bochner integral in tiltExcess.)

10. Hoelder estimate. campanato applies to g := Du (continuous on B_{gamma_1 rho + s_gamma}(0), which is contained in B_{gamma' rho}(0) inside Omega), r := gamma_1 rho, s_0 := s_gamma, A >= 0 as in step 9 and alpha := alpha' > 0. For x, y in B_{gamma_1 rho}(0) with |x - y| <= s_gamma/2 it gives |Du(x) - Du(y)| <= (2^(2n+2+2 alpha') A/omega_n)^(1/2) |x - y|^alpha' = C_Hol delta^a (|x - y|/rho)^alpha' (as sigma_gamma^(-alpha') = c_sig^(-alpha') rho^(-alpha')). If |x - y| > s_gamma/2, then by step 8 |Du(x) - Du(y)| <= 2 C_D delta^a <= 2 C_D delta^a (2|x - y|/s_gamma)^alpha' = 2 C_D (2/c_s)^alpha' delta^a (|x - y|/rho)^alpha'.

11. Conclusion. On the closed ball B_{gamma_1 rho}(0), which is contained in Omega: |u(x)| <= C_H delta^a |x| by (H); hsNorm(Du(x)) <= C_D delta^a by step 8; and hsNorm(Du(x) - Du(y)) <= max{C_Hol, 2 C_D (2/c_s)^alpha'} delta^a (|x - y|/rho)^alpha' by step 10 (Du = fderiv u, u being C^1 on the open set Omega). Since CR is at least each of these constants and the multiplied quantities are nonnegative, the three conclusions hold with CR for every delta in (0, delta_R]; delta_R and CR were chosen in step 1 before U, V, H, delta, rho, q, u.
key_steps: Linear algebra: (Nor), (Ang) and (Gp) for graph planes
Constants before the data; the arbitrary-real witnesses C_II°, C_III° of tilt_iteration are replaced by C_II := max{C_II°, 1}, C_III := max{C_III°, 1}
Conical excess at 0 is O(delta) by (M3); with (E1), (E2) and (Nor) it bounds the weighted L^2 norm of u - Du x
radial_height (constant depending only on n) gives the height bound |u(x)| <= C_H delta^a |x| on the whole ball
